title: Make regressions measurable
purpose: Enable a learner who has shipped an AI feature to turn a vague regression concern into a small, trustworthy binary-labeled evaluation set whose semantics and identity remain stable through judge evaluation and metric calculation.
prerequisites: The learner has shipped or worked with an AI feature and can name an output behavior they consider unacceptable.
The learner can read and edit basic Python literals and run cells in a Jupyter notebook.
No prior evaluation, statistics, LLM-as-judge, or JSONL knowledge is assumed.

user_stories.title: Name the regression before measuring it
user_stories.statement: As an AI feature owner, I want to express one observable failure criterion so that evaluation cases are judged against a shared decision rule rather than intuition.
user_stories.one_idea: A useful eval begins with one observable failure criterion and an explicit decision boundary, not merely a collection of plausible prompts.
acceptance_criteria: The learner-facing section distinguishes an input example from a labeled evaluation case.
The failure criterion is observable from the stored input and candidate output.
The criterion excludes unrelated preferences such as style when style is not the behavior under evaluation.

user_stories.title: Define the positive class
user_stories.statement: As an evaluator, I want labels with an explicit positive-class meaning so that later precision and recall answer the intended regression-detection question.
user_stories.one_idea: Binary labels are meaningful only when the positive class is named and kept invariant; in this course, positive means the candidate output exhibits the defined regression.
acceptance_criteria: The section states that label 1 means regression present and label 0 means acceptable under the selected criterion.
Examples demonstrate that unrelated output qualities do not change the label.
The section previews that precision and recall in EP-03 will measure detection of label 1 without teaching the formulas early.

user_stories.title: Create cases with stable identities
user_stories.statement: As an eval maintainer, I want each human-labeled case to have a stable ID and a minimal schema so that later judge predictions can be aligned without relying on file order.
user_stories.one_idea: Stable case IDs and a small explicit record schema make cumulative evaluation artifacts joinable and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Every record declares case_id, input, candidate_output, and human_label.
Case IDs are unique strings and human_label is restricted to integer 0 or 1.
The persisted file contains examples from both classes and preserves the positive-class convention.

user_stories.title: Validate before automating
user_stories.statement: As an eval maintainer, I want deterministic dataset checks so that malformed or ambiguous records fail before an LLM judge is introduced.
user_stories.one_idea: Fail-fast validation protects every downstream result because an automated judge cannot repair ambiguous labels, duplicate identity, or incomplete records.

checkpoints.capability: Create a small, labeled evaluation set with an explicit positive class and validate its schema and class counts.
checkpoints.observable_check: After completing US-L01-01 through US-L01-04, a fresh-kernel notebook run produces eval_cases.jsonl; validation reports no missing fields, invalid labels, or duplicate IDs, prints counts for labels 0 and 1, and prints an explicit PASS result.

acceptance_criteria: The section connects each validation rule to a concrete downstream failure it prevents.
Validation covers required fields, non-empty unique IDs, allowed binary labels, and representation of both classes.
The learner is prepared to interpret the visible notebook checks rather than treating file creation alone as success.

visible_checks: Print the declared failure criterion and the invariant label mapping: 1 = regression present, 0 = acceptable under that criterion.
After creating the records, print the case count and a preview containing stable case IDs and human labels.
Validate required fields, non-empty unique case IDs, and integer labels restricted to 0 or 1; print actionable errors or PASS.
Print the class counts and fail if either class is absent.
Write eval_cases.jsonl, read it back, compare the reloaded records with the in-memory records, and print the output path plus a final PASS.
build_along.offline_replay: The canonical Jupyter notebook uses only pinned Python 3.12-compatible local dependencies and repository-contained data. From a fresh kernel it creates, validates, writes, and reloads the JSONL artifact without network access, API keys, model weights, or paid calls; the executed notebook and its actual printed output are recorded under output/lesson-01/.

capstone_trace: CP-L01-03-A supplies the capstone's human ground truth: validated records with stable IDs, stored inputs, candidate outputs, and binary human labels.
The invariant positive-class definition (1 = regression present) determines what EP-03 precision and recall measure.

build/lesson-01/eval_cases.jsonl is independently useful as a human-reviewable regression suite and is the required input to EP-02, which must preserve case_id and human_label unchanged when producing judge_predictions.jsonl.
Schema, uniqueness, class-presence, persistence, and round-trip checks reduce the risk that the final grader reports metrics from missing, duplicated, reordered, or semantically inconsistent cases.

This lesson satisfies the first part of the capstone acceptance contract; later epics must add validated judge predictions, compute TP/FP/FN/TN, print precision and recall with explicit zero-division handling, and verify known fixture values.

Searcher brief: research only EP-01 claims needed to distinguish examples from eval cases, define binary positive-class semantics, justify stable IDs and human ground truth, and support fail-fast dataset validation; write only agent/evals-course-factory/output/lesson-01/searcher/sources.json, use real industry vocabulary, and do not research or draft EP-02/EP-03, lesson prose, notebook code, or judge metrics.

Builder brief: consume only this approved plan and approved EP-01 research; write exactly course/lesson-01.md plus the notebook, fixtures, and persisted learner artifact under build/lesson-01/, with actual executed results only under output/lesson-01/. Preserve four text-only, one-idea sections of 300-500 words and about 2-3 minutes each, followed by exactly one incremental build-along of at most 20 minutes. Use an editable Jupyter notebook that runs offline top-to-bottom from a fresh kernel on pinned Python 3.12 dependencies, prints every declared visible check, and persists eval_cases.jsonl. Do not use Mermaid, raster images, quizzes, flashcards, video, audio, paid calls, model weights, or EP-02/EP-03 content; preserve AI-generation provenance in the agent-owned workflow artifacts.
